profile.headline: Controls SWE in Test @ Mathworks
profile.summary:
My name is Gabe and I'm a Mechanical Engineer with a concentration in Dynamic Systems and Control. 

I am interested in developing autonomous systems and have experience designing, modeling, and simulating robotic systems.

positions.title: Global Subsystem Leadership Team Intern
positions.description:
Despite the virtual setting, I deeply enjoyed my time at General Motors.
During my internship, I worked within the Global Subsystem Leadership Team. I started by performing automotive benchmarking to develop an understanding of GM's position among its competitors in the automotive space. Having analyzed new designed trends, I presented recommendations for updates to GM's next-generation vehicle lineup. In parallel, I led technical work-groups to update internal best practices. I ended my summer working alongside advanced vehicle development in order to create an excel-based tool to estimate costs for new projects.

positions.title: Mechanical Design Lead
positions.description:
Over the course of an academic year, I worked on a team to develop a robotic system to explore a subterranean archaeological excavation in Chavin de Huantar, Peru. As electro-mechanical lead, I focused on integrating the mechanical and electrical components of the rover. Principally, I worked on designing a rocker boogies suspension system, implementing the rover's teleoperated control system (using arduino and raspberry pi), and creating a responsive and intuitive user interface (using Javascript, HTML, and CSS).
Following the academic year, I had the opportunity to travel to Chavin de Huantar to deploy the rover. Over the course of 10 weeks, I continued to refine the rover's design to improve its exploration capabilities.
Featured on "Buried Worlds with Don Wildman" on the Travel Channel

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
Project Description: Wearable human motion tracker for monitoring physical therapy and rehabilitation of stroke patients.

Responsibilities:
Analyzed data to validate accuracy of IMU sensors for tracking upper-body human motion
Implemented novel sensor fusion techniques to reduce error in motion tracking algorithm
Collected optical motion capture data
Processed motion capture markers with Cortex for the duration of subject experimentation
Calculated subject joint angles using inverse kinematics

positions.title: Intern
positions.description: I interned as part of the Space division and was tasked with using spacecraft tracking analysis, footprint calculations, and statistical methods to compare data and make a recommendation for a business decision regarding the expansion of the TV footprint to a new location.

positions.title: Intern - Virginia Governor's Mentorships in Engineering
positions.description: I interned at the Atmospheric Science Data Center under the direction of software engineer, Walter Baskin.  I had the opportunity to work on evaluating and benchmarking 3D virtual globe applications for visualization and analysis of four dimensional atmospheric profile data from NASA Earth observing satellites.

positions.title: Student - Youth Leadership Greater Washington
positions.description: I was part of  a six-month, interactive youth leadership development and community education program for high school students that sought to connect youth leaders while raising their awareness of critical regional issues.

positions.title: Intern - Youth Engagement Through Science Program
positions.description: I interned in the museum's department of Paleobiology under the guidance of the curator of Ostracoda, Gene Hunt working on organizing and improving the collection of fossil Ostracodes and analyzing the specimens to study Ostracod dimorphism.

courses.name: Smart Robots in our Mix: Collaborating in High Tech Environments of Tomorrow

honors.title: Donald Kennedy Public Service Fellowship
honors.description: Provided for projects that are student-designed in collaboration with a community partner, student-implemented, have an immediate impact within nine weeks, are sustainable and leave a tangible deliverable with the community partner.
honors.issuer: Issued by Haas Center for Public Service · Mar 2019

honors.title: Scholastic Excellence Award
honors.description: The Scholastic Excellence Award enforces the tough and smart image of the Marine Corps by recognizing noteworthy academic achievements, as well as leadership excellence. The purpose of this award is to recognize a student who has most excelled in academic achievement and has maintained the leadership standards of a high school scholar.

volunteerExperiences.description: I mentored students from East Palo Alto High School and Menlo Atherton High School, providing academic support for math and science classes as well as advice for navigating the college admission process.
Peer Helping is a program at Westfield High School where students are given the opportunity to visit local elementary schools are work with children to overcome their academic and personal hardships.
